title: Population Transformer: Learning Population-level Representations of Neural Activity
goal: Surpass the source-paper result on the same task: Binary word-volume decoding on the paper’s original Volume endpoint: distinguish top versus bottom RMS-intensity quartiles within each recording. This original endpoint is within the registration’s volume/speech/sentence scope; a result claims this endpoint only. Retain the original Volume electrode-count analysis alongside the 90-electrode Table 1 primary.
primary_outputs: Candidate method and outputs for the source task: Binary word-volume decoding on the paper’s original Volume endpoint: distinguish top versus bottom RMS-intensity quartiles within each recording. This original endpoint is within the registration’s volume/speech/sentence scope; a result claims this endpoint only. Retain the original Volume electrode-count analysis alongside the 90-electrode Table 1 primary.

Source-paper comparison for Table 1 Volume ROC-AUC, BrainBERT inputs, 90 electrodes, mean across seven subjects: Within each participant compute ROC-AUC, equivalently P(score_positive>score_negative)+0.5 P(tie), then source aggregation. Higher is better. F1 and local PopT-minus-linear gains do not replace the absolute PopT source score.
success_criteria: Bind the original 90-electrode Table 1 Volume task for all seven participants, including source random-row partitions, labels, BrainBERT features and pretrained access.
Exceed 0.87 published subject-mean ROC-AUC and a calibrated matched pretrained-PopT rerun by a justified predeclared effect with uncertainty.
Freeze candidate after original training/validation development and before complete original test scoring.
Report new chronological/support-disjoint splits, fewer electrodes, alternate tasks or narrowed participants as extensions; none establishes Table 1 victory.

Retain the Figure 3 Volume analysis at all original 1, 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 electrode counts and its four source comparator curves; recover numerical curves and predeclare how count effects constrain the claim. The 90-electrode primary does not license omitting registered electrode-count effects.
The bound improvement contract must be improvement_ready and its complete same-task comparison and admission requirements must pass.
Reproduction is calibration only; reconstructing a numerical result, changing the task or split, or achieving stronger significance alone is not success.

episode.improvement_loop: After historical binding, use the original training/validation rows for candidate development; train-only channel ranking must be reconciled with the historical recipe rather than silently changed.

episode.final_evaluation: Evaluate complete original test rows with author ROC-AUC per subject and source mean aggregation; retain shared-stimulus and temporal uncertainty. Report the complete original Figure 3 Volume electrode-count conditions and comparators alongside the 90-electrode primary.
episode.baseline_policy: The stronger-than-paper comparator is pretrained PopT+BrainBERT at 90 channels. Linear/deep concatenation baselines remain calibration controls; new support-disjoint evaluation is separately labeled extension. Where the source protocol itself uses stochastic draws, a faithful rerun may use declared provenance, a justified reproduction tolerance and paired candidate-author draws; fixed source partitions and full original condition support must remain unchanged.
